passage:
A student using a wheelchair helped create a map of accessible routes around school. The official map showed ramps, but it did not show steep slopes, broken pavement, or doors that were hard to open.
Her map included real experience.
After teachers saw it, the school fixed several problem areas and changed event routes.
Students learned that accessibility is not only about meeting minimum rules. It is about whether people can actually move with safety and dignity.
A map made from lived experience can reveal barriers that planners miss. The best design listens to the people who use it every day.
